identification.summary: UAT-8302 is Cisco Talos's designation for a China-nexus advanced persistent threat cluster that Talos reported on 2026-05-05 as targeting government entities in South America and southeastern Europe with a mix of custom malware shared with other China-nexus clusters and open-source tools [S1][S2].
identification.notes: UAT-* is Cisco Talos's uncategorized-threat naming; Microsoft has no known mapping in the sources reviewed. Talos reportedly links UAT-8302 malware to previously disclosed clusters (Jewelbug / REF7707 / CL-STA-0049, LongNosedGoblin / ESET, and Erudite Mogwai for CloudSorcerer), which indicates shared tooling, not that these are the same actor; keep vendor cluster boundaries separate [S1][S2]. Details come from search-result summaries of the Talos post and secondary coverage; the Talos post could not be opened.

attribution.sponsor: China-nexus (state sponsor or specific organization not named in reviewed sources)
attribution.confidence: Talos assesses with high confidence that UAT-8302 is a China-nexus APT (vendor assessment, per secondary summaries) [S1][S2]
attribution.basis: Talos cites malware overlap with other China-nexus clusters (NetDraft/FINALDRAFT-SquidDoor family, CloudSorcerer, VShell/SNOWLIGHT) and a suggested close operating relationship among those clusters [S1][S2]. This is a vendor assessment; no government attribution was found.

objectives: Talos assesses the group is tasked primarily with obtaining and maintaining long-term access to government and related entities; observed post-compromise activity centered on information collection, credential extraction and spread within the network [S1][S2].

targeting.notes: South American government targeting since at least late 2024; southeastern European government agencies during 2025 [S2]. Specific victim countries and agencies were not identified in the sources reviewed.

capabilities.summary: Custom malware includes NetDraft (a .NET/C# backdoor described as a variant of the FINALDRAFT/SquidDoor family, also reported by ESET as NosyDoor), CloudSorcerer version 3, the VShell backdoor with the SNOWLIGHT stager, and SNOWRUST, a Rust-based stager that downloads and executes VShell [S1][S2][S3]. Open-source tooling includes Impacket and proxying tools [S2][S3]. Initial access method is not known; exploitation of web application vulnerabilities is suspected [S1][S2].

campaigns.name: South America government intrusions
campaigns.summary: Earliest activity Talos attributes to UAT-8302, against government organizations in South America [S2].

campaigns.name: Southeastern Europe government intrusions
campaigns.summary: Activity against government agencies in southeastern Europe throughout 2025, using shared China-nexus malware families [S2].

campaigns.name: Talos public disclosure
campaigns.summary: Talos published 'UAT-8302 and its box full of malware' describing the cluster, its toolset and links to other China-nexus clusters [S1].

diamond.adversary: China-nexus APT tracked by Cisco Talos as UAT-8302; sponsor not named; shares tooling with other China-nexus clusters [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: NetDraft, CloudSorcerer v3, VShell, SNOWLIGHT/SNOWRUST, Impacket, proxying tools [S2][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: Remote servers hosting VShell payloads fetched by SNOWRUST [S2]. Specific IPs/domains were not captured.
diamond.victim: Government entities in South America and southeastern Europe [S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: Long-term access collection against government networks consistent with state-aligned espionage tasking, per Talos's tasking assessment [S1]. Specific policy drivers not stated in the sources.
diamond.technology: Likely internet-facing web applications as suspected entry points [S1]; further victim technology details not verified.

gaps: The primary Talos report could not be opened (fetch failed); details are from search-result summaries and secondary coverage, so per-claim source mapping is approximate.
Initial access vector unconfirmed (web application exploitation suspected only).
Victim countries and agencies not named.

Exact relationship to Jewelbug/REF7707/CL-STA-0049, LongNosedGoblin and Erudite Mogwai is unresolved; shared malware does not establish identity. One aggregator also cited shared infrastructure with Earth Estries and UNC5174, unconfirmed.
No Microsoft name, MITRE group ID or government attribution found.
IOCs and detection content not reviewed.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Step 1-2: government networks in South America and southeastern Europe, including partner-nation networks, are the observed battlespace [S2]. Step 3: adversary tooling is shared across China-nexus clusters, so detections should not be keyed to one actor name [S1]. MLCOA: continued long-term access and credential collection from government networks. MDCOA: expansion to additional regions or reuse of footholds for broader access. Candidate indicators: Impacket activity, proxying tools, Rust stagers pulling VShell [S2][S3].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: track Talos and ESET reporting on the shared China-nexus malware families and push indicators to partner-nation cyber contacts. Authorities: any hunt on partner or allied networks requires host-nation consent and coordination. Mission assurance: harden AD, restrict proxying tools, and patch internet-facing web apps. Coordination: share findings through intelligence and CERT channels.
